Count the actions of each actor and session in an event log

Source: R/multilevel.R
event_frequencies.Rd

event_frequencies() counts how often each action occurred in each occasion of an event log, where an occasion is an actor, or an actor's session. This table of action frequencies is what a network of actions, which shows which actions tend to occur together in the same occasion, is estimated from.

In an event log each row records one action by one actor, such as a student reading, taking a quiz or writing a note; behavioural and learning data often arrive in this form. Occasions are formed by actor, by actor and session when sessions are given, and, with time and compute_sessions = TRUE, by splitting an actor's events into sessions wherever the gap between consecutive events exceeds time_threshold.

The result is a data frame with one row per occasion and one column per distinct action, holding the count.

psychnet() performs this conversion itself when given an event log, so the function is needed only to inspect or reuse the table. Events with a missing or empty action are not counted.

Usage

event_frequencies(
  data,
  actor = "Actor",
  action = "Action",
  session = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  compute_sessions = TRUE,
  time_threshold = 900
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per event.

actor

Column(s) identifying the actor. Default "Actor".

action

Column holding the action. Default "Action".

session

Optional column(s) identifying sessions within an actor.

time

Optional column of event times (numbers, dates, date-times or timestamps as text), used only to split sessions.

compute_sessions

Whether to split each actor's events into sessions at gaps in time longer than time_threshold. Default TRUE; has no effect without time.

time_threshold

Longest gap between consecutive events within one session, in the units of time (seconds for date-times). Default 900 (15 minutes).

Value

A data frame with one row per occasion and columns actor, session (an occasion label joining the actor, the session and, when sessions are computed from time, the session number, separated by ".") and one numeric column of counts per action.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when data is not a data frame, a named column is missing, action has fewer than two distinct values, actor or session has missing values, or time cannot be read as numbers or timestamps.

See also

psychnet() with actor to estimate a network from an event log; psychnet_multilevel for within-actor and between-actor networks.

Examples

ev <- data.frame(
  Actor   = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 6),
  Session = rep(rep(1:2, each = 3), 2),
  Action  = c("read","quiz","read", "quiz","read","note",
              "note","note","read", "read","quiz","quiz"))
event_frequencies(ev, session = "Session")
#>   actor session note quiz read
#> 1     a     a.1    0    1    2
#> 2     a     a.2    1    1    1
#> 3     b     b.1    2    0    1
#> 4     b     b.2    0    2    1
